added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).  All expectations in this proof are under \(P\).  The model definition \(\mathrm{def:exact\mbox{-}model}\), together with \(\kappa=0\), gives the known design density \(1\) on \(D=[0,1]^d\),
\[
 \frac14\leq e(x)=\frac{g_P(x)}4\leq\frac12,
 \qquad e\in\mathcal H_d^\alpha(L/4),
 \qquad \mu_0\in\mathcal H_d^\beta(L),
 \qquad \tau\in\mathcal H_d^\gamma(L),
 \tag{1}
\]
and the Bernoulli response law with \(\mu_1=\mu_0+\tau\).  In particular, \(|\tau|\leq3/4\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\) gives independence of the observations used below.

Let \(m_s=\lceil s\rceil-1\) and choose
\[
 p=m_\gamma+\max\{m_\alpha,m_\beta\}.
\]
For a positive integer \(M\), partition \(D\) into the \(M^d\) half-open cubes of side \(M^{-1}\), with the usual closure convention on the upper faces.  Let \(\mathcal B_M\) be the space of functions whose restriction to each cell is a polynomial of total degree at most \(p\).  Thus
\[
 K_M=\dim(\mathcal B_M)=a_pM^d,
 \qquad a_p=\binom{p+d}{d}<\infty.
 \tag{2}
\]
On each cell, scaled tensor Legendre polynomials indexed by multi-indices of total degree at most \(p\), extended by zero off that cell, give a completely explicit Lebesgue-orthonormal basis \(b_M:D\to\mathbb R^{K_M}\).  Therefore its exact Gram matrix is
\[
 \Omega_M=\int_D b_M(z)b_M(z)^\top\,dz=I_{K_M}.
 \tag{3}
\]
This is a genuinely finite-dimensional space: the polynomial degree is at most \(p\).

For the tuning proxy \(k\geq1\), set \(M=M_0+\lfloor k^{1/d}\rfloor\), where the fixed integer \(M_0\) will be chosen below, and abbreviate \(b_k=b_M\), \(K_k=K_M\), and \(\Pi_k\) for the orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal B_M\) in \(L_2(D,dz)\).  Equation (2) implies
\[
 K_k\leq Ck,
 \qquad M^{-1}\leq Ck^{-1/d}.
 \tag{4}
\]
This is the promised rank rounding.  Repeated one-dimensional Taylor expansion along coordinate segments, using exactly the derivative and top-order H\"older bounds in the definition of \(\mathcal H_d^s(L)\), shows that on a physical cell of side \(h/M\) the Taylor polynomial of degree \(m_s\) has uniform remainder at most \(C(h/M)^s\).  Projecting cannot have larger \(L_2\) error than this explicit cellwise polynomial approximant.  Since multiplication by any fixed polynomial of degree at most \(m_\gamma\) keeps the resulting cellwise degree at most \(p\), we obtain, for every component \(v_j\) of a fixed polynomial basis \(v\) introduced below,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \|(I-\Pi_k)\{v_j(e(h\,\cdot)-3/8)\}\|_2&\leq C\ell^\alpha,\\
 \|(I-\Pi_k)(\mu_0(h\,\cdot)-1/2)\|_2&\leq C\ell^\beta,\\
 \|(I-\Pi_k)\{e(h\,\cdot)v_j\}\|_2&\leq C\ell^\alpha,
 \end{split}
 \qquad \ell=hk^{-1/d}.
 \tag{5}
\]
The argument includes \(s\leq1\), when the cellwise approximant is constant.  All constants in (5) are uniform over the model because the radii in (1) are fixed.

Let \(v:D\to\mathbb R^q\) be a fixed Lebesgue-orthonormal basis of polynomials of total degree at most \(m_\gamma\), where \(q=\binom{m_\gamma+d}{d}\).  Define
\[
 Q=\int_Dv(z)v(z)^\top e(hz)\{1-e(hz)\}\,dz,
 \qquad
 R=\int_Dv(z)e(hz)\{1-e(hz)\}\tau(hz)\,dz,
 \tag{6}
\]
\(\theta=Q^{-1}R\), and \(\tau_h(hz)=v(z)^\top\theta\).  By (1) and orthonormality of \(v\),
\[
 \frac{3}{16}I_q\preceq Q\preceq\frac14I_q.
 \tag{7}
\]
Thus \(Q\) is invertible and \(\theta\), \(v\), and \(\tau_h\) are uniformly bounded.  Let \(T_\tau\) be the order-\(m_\gamma\) Taylor polynomial of \(\tau\) at the corner.  The same coordinatewise Taylor argument used for (5) gives
\[
 \sup_{z\in D}|\tau(hz)-T_\tau(hz)|\leq Ch^\gamma.
 \tag{8}
\]
Because \(T_\tau(h\,\cdot)\) belongs to the span of \(v\), equations (6)--(8) and \(\|Q^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq16/3\) yield
\[
 |\tau_h(0)-\tau(0)|
 \leq \|v(0)\|\,\|Q^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \left\|\int_Dv(z)e(hz)\{1-e(hz)\}\{\tau(hz)-T_\tau(hz)\}\,dz\right\|
 \leq Ch^\gamma.
 \tag{9}
\]

We now define the estimator.  Use the fixed bounded pilots
\[
 \bar e(x)=3/8,
 \qquad \bar\mu(x)=1/2.
 \tag{10}
\]
For \(x\in[0,1]^d\), put \(w_h(x)=h^{-d}\mathbf1\{x\in hD\}\), \(v_h(x)=v(x/h)\mathbf1\{x\in hD\}\), and \(b_{h,k}(x)=b_k(x/h)\mathbf1\{x\in hD\}\).  For \(o=(x,a,y)\), define
\[
 \phi_{a1}(o)=a\{a-\bar e(x)\},
 \qquad
 \phi_{y1}(o)=\{y-\bar\mu(x)\}\{a-\bar e(x)\},
 \tag{11}
\]
and, for \(o_r=(x_r,a_r,y_r)\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 \phi_{a2}(o_1,o_2)
 &=-\{a_1-\bar e(x_1)\}
 b_{h,k}(x_1)^\top\Omega_M^{-1}b_{h,k}(x_2)a_2,\\
 \phi_{y2}(o_1,o_2)
 &=-\{a_1-\bar e(x_1)\}
 b_{h,k}(x_1)^\top\Omega_M^{-1}b_{h,k}(x_2)
 \{y_2-\bar\mu(x_2)\}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{12}
\]
For \(\mathbb P_n f=n^{-1}\sum_i f(O_i)\) and \(\mathbb U_nH=\{n(n-1)\}^{-1}\sum_{i\ne j}H(O_i,O_j)\), set
\[
 \begin{split}
 \widetilde Q={}&\mathbb P_n\!\left[
 w_h(X)v_h(X)\phi_{a1}(O)v_h(X)^\top\right]\\
 &+\mathbb U_n\!\left[
 w_h(X_1)w_h(X_2)v_h(X_1)phi_{a2}(O_1,O_2)v_h(X_2)^\top\right],\\
 \widetilde R={}&\mathbb P_n\!\left[
 w_h(X)v_h(X)\phi_{y1}(O)\right]\\
 &+\mathbb U_n\!\left[
 w_h(X_1)w_h(X_2)v_h(X_1)\phi_{y2}(O_1,O_2)\right].
 \end{split}
 \tag{13}
\]
The second observation's factor \(v_h(X_2)^\top\) in the correction to \(\widetilde Q\) is essential: it makes the cancellation below exact.  The matrix \(\widetilde Q\) need not be symmetric, so stabilization is performed on singular values rather than on eigenvalues.

Let \(\lambda_0=3/16\).  Choose a deterministic Borel singular-value decomposition \(\widetilde Q=U\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_q)V^\top\), with a fixed lexicographic tie rule, and define
\[
 \widetilde Q_{\mathrm{fl}}
 =U\operatorname{diag}(s_1\vee\lambda_0/2,\ldots,s_q\vee\lambda_0/2)V^\top.
 \tag{14}
\]
Finally set
\[
 \widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)
 =\operatorname{clip}_{[-3/4,3/4]}
 \left\{v(0)^\top\widetilde Q_{\mathrm{fl}}^{-1}\widetilde R\right\}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) and (10)--(15) use only fixed polynomial evaluations, exact Lebesgue integrals, sample averages, an ordered finite \(U\)-statistic, finite matrix operations, singular-value flooring, and clipping.  Hence (15) is a total Borel map on every sample; in particular, no inverse propensity and no nonempty-cell event is required.

It remains to prove its risk.  Write \(\delta_e=e-\bar e\), \(\delta_\mu=\mu_0-\bar\mu\), and use a superscript \(h\) for stretching to \(D\), for example \(\delta_e^h(z)=\delta_e(hz)\).  Put \(\widetilde S=\widetilde R-\widetilde Q\theta\).  Conditional Bernoulli expectations from \(\mathrm{def:exact\mbox{-}model}\) give, equation by equation,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathbb E[\phi_{y1}(O)\mid X=x]
 &=e(x)\{1-\bar e(x)\}\tau(x)+\delta_e(x)\delta_\mu(x),\\
 \mathbb E[\phi_{a1}(O)\mid X=x]
 &=e(x)\{1-\bar e(x)\},\\
 \mathbb E[\phi_{y2}(O_1,O_2)\mid X_1=x_1,X_2=x_2]
 &=-\delta_e(x_1)b_{h,k}(x_1)^\top\Omega_M^{-1}b_{h,k}(x_2)
 \{\delta_\mu(x_2)+e(x_2)\tau(x_2)\},\\
 \mathbb E[\phi_{a2}(O_1,O_2)\mid X_1=x_1,X_2=x_2]
 &=-\delta_e(x_1)b_{h,k}(x_1)^\top\Omega_M^{-1}b_{h,k}(x_2)e(x_2).
 \end{split}
 \tag{16}
\]
Changing variables \(x_r=hz_r\) in (13), using (3), and subtracting \(\widetilde Q\theta\), equation (16) yields for each coordinate \(j\)
\[
 \mathbb E\widetilde S_j
 =\int_Dv_j(z)\delta_e^h(z)(I-\Pi_k)
 \left[\delta_\mu^h+e^h\{\tau^h-\tau_h^h\}\right](z)\,dz.
 \tag{17}
\]
Since \((I-\Pi_k)f\) is orthogonal to \(\mathcal B_M\), (17), Cauchy--Schwarz, (5), (8)--(9), and contraction of an orthogonal projection give
\[
 \begin{split}
 |\mathbb E\widetilde S_j|
 &=\left|\int_D(I-\Pi_k)(v_j\delta_e^h)
 (I-\Pi_k)\left[\delta_\mu^h+e^h\{\tau^h-\tau_h^h\}\right]dz\right|\\
 &\leq C\ell^\alpha\{\ell^\beta+h^\gamma\}
 =C\{\ell^S+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{18}
\]
This proves the two nuisance-related bias terms without imposing any smoothness on \(\mathbb E[Y\mid X]\).

The same calculation controls the mean of the corrected matrix.  For coordinates \(j,r\), (16) and (6) imply
\[
 \{\mathbb E\widetilde Q-Q\}_{jr}
 =\int_Dv_j\delta_e^h(I-\Pi_k)(e^hv_r)\,dz
 =\int_D(I-\Pi_k)(v_j\delta_e^h)(I-\Pi_k)(e^hv_r)\,dz.
 \tag{19}
\]
Consequently the direct cell-width version of (5) gives
\[
 \|\mathbb E\widetilde Q-Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq C(h/M)^{2\alpha}
 \leq CM_0^{-2\alpha};
 \qquad
 \|\mathbb E\widetilde Q-Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq C\ell^{2\alpha}.
 \tag{20}
\]
Choose the fixed \(M_0\) so that the last bound is at most \(\lambda_0/4\).  By (7), the smallest singular value of \(\mathbb E\widetilde Q\) is then at least \(3\lambda_0/4\).

We next derive every variance term.  Because \(\mathbb P_nf=\mathbb U_n[f(O_1)]\), each coordinate of \(\widetilde S\) is an ordered second-order \(U\)-statistic.  Symmetrizing its kernel does not change the statistic.  Direct enumeration of pairs of index pairs gives, for any square-integrable symmetric kernel \(\xi\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\{\mathbb U_n\xi\}
 \leq\frac4n\mathbb E\left[\mathbb E\{\xi(O_1,O_2)\mid O_1\}^2\right]
 +\frac{2}{n(n-1)}\mathbb E\{\xi(O_1,O_2)^2\}.
 \tag{21}
\]
Indeed, terms indexed by disjoint pairs have zero covariance by \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\); at most \(4n(n-1)(n-2)\) ordered pair-pairs share one index, and at most \(2n(n-1)\) share two, after division by \(n^2(n-1)^2\).

The one-observation part of the kernel has second moment at most
\[
 C\int_{hD}h^{-2d}\,dx=Ch^{-d}.
 \tag{22}
\]
For the two-observation part, \(A,Y\), the pilots, and the fixed \(v\)-factors are bounded, while \(b_k\) is controlled by the displayed Hilbert--Schmidt calculation
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\int_D\int_D
 \left\{b_k(z_1)^\top\Omega_M^{-1}b_k(z_2)\right\}^2\,dz_1\,dz_2\\
 &\qquad=\operatorname{tr}\left(
 \Omega_M^{-1}\Omega_M\Omega_M^{-1}\Omega_M\right)
 =K_k\leq Ck.
 \end{split}
 \tag{23}
\]
Two local weights and the two changes of variables therefore give
\[
 \mathbb E\{\xi(O_1,O_2)^2\}\leq C\{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\}.
 \tag{24}
\]
For a one-index projection of the two-observation term, integration over the other observation produces \(\Pi_k\) applied either to \(\delta_\mu^h+e^h(\tau^h-\tau_h^h)\) or to a bounded fixed-polynomial multiple of \(e^h\).  The \(L_2\) contraction \(\|\Pi_k f\|_2\leq\|f\|_2\), followed by one remaining localization, gives
\[
 \mathbb E\left[\mathbb E\{\xi(O_1,O_2)\mid O_1\}^2\right]\leq Ch^{-d},
 \tag{25}
\]
and the same bound holds for the projection on \(O_2\).  Combining (21)--(25), and recalling that \(q\) is fixed, proves
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widetilde S-\mathbb E\widetilde S\|^2
 \leq C\left\{\frac1{nh^d}+\frac{k}{n^2h^{2d}}\right\}.
 \tag{26}
\]
The identical calculation for every entry of \(\widetilde Q\), with the last factor in (12) replaced by the bounded quantity \(A_2v_h(X_2)\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widetilde Q-\mathbb E\widetilde Q\|_{\mathrm F}^2
 \leq C\left\{\frac1{nh^d}+\frac{k}{n^2h^{2d}}\right\}.
 \tag{27}
\]
Set
\[
 u=\left\{\frac1{nh^d}+\frac{k}{n^2h^{2d}}\right\}^{1/2}.
 \tag{28}
\]
If \(u\) exceeds a sufficiently small fixed constant, clipping and \(|\tau(0)|\leq3/4\) give the desired inequality after increasing \(C\).  Suppose therefore that \(u\) is below that constant, and let
\[
 \mathcal G=\{\|\widetilde Q-\mathbb E\widetilde Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\lambda_0/4\}.
\]
Equations (7), (20), (27), and Markov's inequality imply
\[
 \mathbb P(\mathcal G^c)\leq Cu^2\leq Cu,
 \tag{29}
\]
while on \(\mathcal G\), the smallest singular value of \(\widetilde Q\) is at least \(\lambda_0/2\).  Hence singular-value flooring is inactive on \(\mathcal G\), and
\[
 \begin{split}
 \left|v(0)^\top\widetilde Q^{-1}\widetilde R-\tau_h(0)\right|
 &=\left|v(0)^\top\widetilde Q^{-1}(\widetilde R-\widetilde Q\theta)\right|\\
 &\leq (2/\lambda_0)\|v(0)\|\,\|\widetilde S\|.
 \end{split}
 \tag{30}
\]
Clipping is a contraction toward \(\tau(0)\in[-3/4,3/4]\).  Thus (9), (18), (26), (29), (30), and Cauchy--Schwarz yield
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathbb E\left|\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)-\tau(0)\right|
 &\leq Ch^\gamma+C\|\mathbb E\widetilde S\|
 +C\{\mathbb E\|\widetilde S-\mathbb E\widetilde S\|^2\}^{1/2}
 +\frac32\mathbb P(\mathcal G^c)\\
 &\leq C\left\{h^\gamma+\ell^S+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha
 +(nh^d)^{-1/2}+\frac{\sqrt{k}}{nh^d}\right\}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{31}
\]
Since \(0<\ell\leq1\), \(h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\leq h^\gamma\).  Also \(a+b\leq\sqrt{2(a^2+b^2)}\) for \(a,b\geq0\); applying this with \(a=(nh^d)^{-1/2}\) and \(b=\sqrt{k}/(nh^d)\) gives the second displayed bound in the statement.  Every constant used above is uniform in \(P\), so taking the supremum completes the proof.
added_lemmas.justification: This lemma supplies the feasible, total higher-order data-only estimator and the finite-sample bias--variance inequality needed to improve the exact-uniform bounded-overlap upper bound.
added_lemmas.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE analyzes the analogous interior bounded-overlap construction under high-level Gram and covariate-law conditions; here the exact uniform law makes the projection Gram known, while the one-sided corner localization, total stabilization, and same-class uniform risk calculation must be established explicitly.
added_lemmas.consumer: The minimax corollary uses this computable estimator to establish an improved sufficient nuisance-smoothness threshold for oracle-rate attainment on the bounded-overlap slice.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(\kappa=0\), set \(S=\alpha+\beta\),
\[
 S_\star=\frac{d\gamma}{2\gamma+d},
 \qquad
 D_\star=1+\frac{d}{2\gamma}+\frac{d}{2S}.
\]
Then every \(P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) satisfies
\[
 e_P(x)=g_P(x)/4\in[1/4,1/2]
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.
\]
There are constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), such that for every \(n\geq2\),
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \leq R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C\max\left\{
 n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
 n^{-1/D_\star}
 \right\}.
\]
The upper bound is attained by the total data-only second-order estimator of \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}risk}\) with explicitly rounded rank and deterministic bandwidth.  Consequently, if \(S\geq S_\star\), then
\[
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
\]
There is no logarithmic multiplier at \(S=S_\star\): the two finite algebraic balances agree there.  If \(S<S_\star\), the theorem gives the displayed upper bound \(Cn^{-1/D_\star}\) and the supplied-propensity lower bound, but does not assert a matching nuisance-dominated lower bound.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:local\mbox{-}propensity\mbox{-}shape}\), \(e_P=r_0g_P/4\), and the definition of \(r_\kappa\) gives \(r_0=1\).  The envelope \(\mathrm{ass:multiplier\mbox{-}envelope}\) therefore gives
\[
 e_P(x)=\frac{g_P(x)}4,
 \qquad
 \frac14\leq e_P(x)\leq\frac12
 \quad(x\in\mathcal X).
 \tag{32}
\]
Thus this is the original exact model restricted to its bounded-overlap parameter slice; neither its uniform support nor any law has been replaced.

For the lower bound, let \(T\) be any data-only Borel estimator and define \(T^e(o_{1:n},e)=T(o_{1:n})\).  This is an admissible oracle estimator that ignores the supplied propensity and has the same loss under every \(P\).  The two minimax definitions \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}risk}\) and \(\mathrm{def:unknown\mbox{-}risk}\) consequently imply
\[
 R_n^e(d,0,\beta,\gamma,L)\leq
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L).
 \tag{33}
\]
The supplied-propensity lower bound in \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}minimax}\), specialized to \(\kappa=0\), and (33) yield
\[
 c_en^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \leq R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \qquad(n\geq2).
 \tag{34}
\]

It remains to tune the estimator in \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}risk}\).  First suppose \(S<S_\star\).  Put
\[
 h_n=n^{-1/(\gamma D_\star)},
 \qquad
 \bar k_n=n^{(d/S-d/\gamma)/D_\star},
 \qquad
 k_n=\max\{1,\lfloor\bar k_n\rfloor\}.
 \tag{35}
\]
Because \(S<S_\star<\gamma\), the exponent of \(\bar k_n\) is positive; integer rounding changes it only by constants.  With \(\ell_n=h_nk_n^{-1/d}\), direct substitution gives
\[
 h_n^\gamma=n^{-1/D_\star},
 \qquad
 \ell_n^S
 \asymp n^{-S/(\gamma D_\star)}
 n^{-(1-S/\gamma)/D_\star}
 =n^{-1/D_\star},
 \tag{36}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{k_n}}{nh_n^d}
 \asymp n^{-1+(d/(2S)+d/(2\gamma))/D_\star}
 =n^{-1/D_\star}.
 \tag{37}
\]
Moreover, \(S<S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\) is equivalent to
\[
 D_\star-\frac d\gamma
 =1-\frac{d}{2\gamma}+\frac{d}{2S}>2.
\]
Hence
\[
 (nh_n^d)^{-1/2}
 =n^{-(D_\star-d/\gamma)/(2D_\star)}
 \leq n^{-1/D_\star}.
 \tag{38}
\]
Equations (35)--(38) and the lemma prove
\[
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\leq Cn^{-1/D_\star}
 \qquad(S<S_\star).
 \tag{39}
\]

Now suppose \(S\geq S_\star\).  Choose
\[
 h_n=n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)},
 \qquad
 k_n=\max\{1,\lfloor nh_n^d\rfloor\}.
 \tag{40}
\]
Then \(k_n\asymp nh_n^d=n^{2\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), so
\[
 h_n^\gamma=n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
 \qquad
 \sqrt{\frac1{nh_n^d}\left(1+\frac{k_n}{nh_n^d}\right)}
 \asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
 \tag{41}
\]
Furthermore \(\ell_n=h_nk_n^{-1/d}\asymp n^{-1/d}\), and therefore
\[
 \ell_n^S\lesssim n^{-S/d}
 \leq n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
 \tag{42}
\]
where the last inequality is exactly \(S\geq S_\star\).  The lemma, (40)--(42), and the definition of the minimax infimum prove the oracle-rate upper bound in this regime.  The estimator remains total for every \(n\); the fixed rank rounding and any finitely many small values of \(n\) are absorbed by enlarging \(C\), since clipping bounds the loss by \(3/2\).

Combining (39) with the high-smoothness bound gives, in all regimes,
\[
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C\max\left\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\right\}.
 \tag{43}
\]
At \(S=S_\star\),
\[
 D_\star
 =1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac{2\gamma+d}{2\gamma}
 =2+\frac d\gamma,
 \qquad
 \frac1{D_\star}=\frac\gamma{2\gamma+d}.
 \tag{44}
\]
Thus (34) and (43) match whenever \(S\geq S_\star\).  Equation (44) also proves the no-logarithm assertion at equality: the proof balances finitely many pure powers at a single bandwidth and rank, and contains no harmonic or multiscale sum.  For \(S<S_\star\), (34) and (39) are the asserted honest bracket; no nuisance-dominated converse has been inferred.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the strongest proved exact-uniform bounded-overlap result: a second-order upper rate in every nuisance regime and the sharp oracle rate once \(\alpha+\beta\ge d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\).
added_lemmas.gap: When \(\alpha+\beta<d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), the upper exponent is proved but a matching nuisance-dominated lower experiment on the singleton uniform design is still missing; the theorem therefore retains only the supplied-propensity lower bound there.
added_lemmas.consumer: Researchers assessing local CATE precision under bounded overlap can use the certified threshold and estimator to identify a regime where rough propensity and control regressions still permit oracle-rate pointwise estimation, without attributing the result to an unmodified causal forest.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The old first-order bracket is strictly superseded on the same exact model by the proved second-order estimator and its sharper threshold; deletion with a replacement migrates every inbound dependency atomically.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: The causal target remains \(\tau_P(0)\).  For arbitrary \(\kappa\geq0\), the total first-order functional \(\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)\) from \(\mathrm{thm:first\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\) gives, with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}\mathbb E_P\lvert\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)-\tau_P(0)\rvert\leq Cn^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}.\]  On the bounded-overlap slice \(\kappa=0\), put \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2S)\).  The total second-order functional \(\widehat\tau_{n,h,k}^{(2)}(0)\) constructed in \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}risk}\), with the deterministic tuning in \(\mathrm{thm:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order}\), satisfies \[c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\leq R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\leq C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\}.\]  The bounds match, with no logarithmic multiplier at equality, whenever \(S\geq S_\star\).  For \(S<S_\star\), the second-order upper exponent is established but its matching exact-uniform nuisance lower bound remains open; for \(\kappa>0\), the sharper higher-order frontier remains open.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The functional metadata must name the new total second-order estimator, its proved tuning map and bounded-overlap threshold, while retaining the established first-order statement for the unresolved local-zero regimes.

prose_updates.tldr: For the exact local-zero model, the proved supplied-propensity lower bound and total first-order estimator retain the all-\(\kappa\) bracket.  On the exact-uniform bounded-overlap slice \(\kappa=0\), a new total second-order local-polynomial \(U\)-statistic estimator improves the upper bound to \(C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\}\).  This proves the sharp pure-power oracle rate whenever \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), including equality with no logarithm.  Below that elbow only the matching exact-uniform nuisance lower bound remains open; for \(\kappa>0\), the higher-order upper/lower frontier and critical logarithms remain open.

project_justification.gap: The closest published pointwise CATE frontier proves a bounded-overlap higher-order rate over a density-qualified class, while its displayed least-favorable density removes nuisance-bump transition regions.  That lower witness does not establish the nuisance-dominated converse on the singleton uniform design, and no published result supplies the full local-zero \(\kappa>0\) frontier.
project_justification.niche: The exactly known uniform covariate law makes the localized projection Gram deterministic and permits a total one-sided second-order estimator without a density-estimation remainder.  This isolates which part of the bounded-overlap frontier transfers constructively and which exact-design converse, corner-power, and tie-surface questions remain genuinely new.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the supplied-propensity benchmark for every \(\kappa\), a total first-order data-only rate on the full class, and a sharper total second-order bound at \(\kappa=0\).  On that exact-uniform slice it proves oracle-rate attainment throughout the certified region \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), including the critical equality without a logarithm, while reporting an honest lower--upper bracket below the elbow rather than asserting the missing nuisance converse.

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, Theorems 1--2 and Definition 2, is the closest bounded-overlap pointwise contrast frontier.  Its higher-order local-polynomial R-learner supplies the architecture adapted here, but its density-qualified lower construction uses perforated support and does not prove the nuisance-dominated lower bound for the singleton uniform design.  The present bounded-overlap lemma derives the one-sided exact-Lebesgue-Gram estimator directly, and the resulting theorem combines its upper bound with Theorem 1's exact-uniform supplied-propensity lower bound to prove sharpness at and above the elbow.  Kennedy2023DRCATE motivates local R-learning, while LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF and ShenGaoWittenHan2020 motivate projection corrections.  RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, requires partition-local perturbations and does not directly cover the overlapping smooth frames needed for the remaining full-support converse.  GaoHan2020 concerns integrated random-design contrast risk; Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesign concerns scalar pointwise regression under a design zero; Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics concerns weak-overlap average-effect inference and scalar regression; and Kim2026RKHSPointwiseCATE retains a global overlap lower bound.  WagerAthey2018CausalForests and GRFReference motivate the application: the official \(\texttt{grf}\) workflow learns nuisance regressions and uses treatment-balance restrictions, but no claim is made that its causal forest implements or attains the estimator proved here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The bounded-overlap higher-order upper calculation is closed, so the remaining \(\kappa=0\) obstruction is only the converse below \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\).  Disjoint partition-local contrast bumps of micro-width \(\ell\) and nuisance-scale amplitude \(\delta=\ell^{\alpha+\beta}\) have H"older scale \(\delta\ell^{-\gamma}=\ell^{\alpha+\beta-\gamma}\), which diverges in the relevant rough regime.  Overlapping smooth squared frames repair transition regularity but violate the partition-local premise of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, and their shared signs generate nonzero multi-observation cross terms; filling perforated transition holes leaves a contribution of order \(nh^d\delta^2\), which diverges at the proposed nuisance rate.  For \(\kappa>0\), the second-order score variance, inverse-overlap geometry, noninteger corner powers, max-norm tie regularity, matching product-mixture lower bound, and possible critical logarithms are all still uncontrolled on the full class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: For arbitrary \(\kappa\geq0\), the established first-order result gives \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\leq R_n\leq Cn^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  At \(\kappa=0\), the proved second-order estimator improves the upper endpoint to \(C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\}\).  This bracket closes to the oracle rate when \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), with no logarithm at equality.  Below the elbow the higher-order upper bound is proved but its nuisance-dominated lower match is not; for \(\kappa>0\), higher-order achievability, the matching converse, the oracle-penalty partition, and critical logarithms remain open.

statement_notes.justification: The explicit estimator and its five-term risk decomposition are the constructive step that lowers the bounded-overlap smoothness threshold from the first-order sufficient condition to the higher-order elbow.
statement_notes.gap: The adaptation removes the published estimator's covariate-Gram estimation condition by using the known uniform law, but it does not import the published perforated-support converse.
statement_notes.consumer: The minimax theorem consumes the lemma's bandwidth--rank tradeoff, and practitioners obtain a total benchmark estimator built from sample moments and finite matrix operations.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem gives the strongest certified exact-uniform bounded-overlap frontier: a higher-order upper bound in all regimes and the exact oracle rate at and above \(S_\star\).
statement_notes.gap: Only the nuisance-dominated exact-uniform lower bound below \(S_\star\) remains open on this slice; no such lower rate is inferred from the supplied-propensity converse.
statement_notes.consumer: Users of local CATE methods can distinguish a proved oracle-rate region from the rough-nuisance region where the computable upper rate is known but information-theoretic sharpness is not.
